title: ext2 direct-write fault/rollback can leave an earlier BIO live
mechanism: InodeInner::write_direct_blocks submits each mapped run into a local IoBatch and only waits after the loop. A user-copy fault on a later run returns through ?, dropping the batch (no Drop, no cancel) with an earlier BIO in flight, after which write_direct_at rolls back and, for extending writes, frees the blocks the live BIO targets.
contract: An I/O syscall that returns (including with EFAULT) has no outstanding device I/O. Linux iomap_dio_rw waits for every submitted BIO, and IoBatch documents that the caller waits for all records it added.
observed: An O_DIRECT pwrite spanning two non-adjacent runs returned EFAULT while the first run's BIO was still in flight and later published 4096 bytes. No later operation was ever clobbered in 64-round and 32-round probes on virtio-blk and NVMe.

repro.how_to_run: Apply specula-initramfs-plumbing.patch to the pin, place the C files in test/initramfs/src/regression/io/specula/, and boot with SMP=2 and SPECULA_INIT pointing at a script that runs them on /ext2 (and /nvme). Cases A/B COMMIT_WITHOUT_REPORT with C NO_PUBLICATION show the mechanism.
repro.runtime_status: MASKED at 604948581 (01a MC-6, SMP=2): mechanism observed in cases A/B/C, harm not observed in D-G, J, J2

caveats: Masked by backend: the mask is a single-worker FIFO staging queue per device plus the blocking wait_all in zero_new_blocks (a debater correction, whereas turn 1 and the 01a handoff name the in-order virtqueue). The write-after-free shape needs a near-full block group. Linux ext4 also returns EFAULT with a committed prefix, so that return alone is not a contract violation. Drivers reference a removed confirmation worktree.
